Here is what I have pieced together about the Bitterfield Unified School District contract (BD-1180).

**Why it went to Bitterfield**

Nathan Porter's email to you on 21 September was candid: he said he did not chase the account — the district's purchasing officer rang him directly and asked for him by name. She did not say why, and he did not ask. The close-out note on the file says "the award has been made on price and service," but Nathan told you that is what those notes always say and he has no idea whether it is the whole reason. So the real driver behind the switch is unknown from our side.

**What is still available**

The three satellite sites were never on the tender and never bid. Glenmont can serve them on the existing Tuesday run — no contract to win, no competitive process. The main district contract renews in the spring, and the branch may bid it at the January list.

---

Here are the options I see for showing a move by the December quarter review:

**Option A — Take the satellite sites now (immediate volume)**

The three satellite sites are open ground. No bid, no tender, no incumbent to displace. We contact the district's purchasing officer directly, offer to supply those sites on the existing Tuesday run, and start billing them this quarter. That puts real revenue back on Glenmont's books before December and shows a concrete recovery of lost ground.

*Tradeoff*: This is the fastest path to visible volume, but it does not recover the main contract. The dollar value of the satellites is smaller.

**Option B — Build the spring bid early (strategic recovery)**

Start preparing a competitive response for the January list now. That means pricing at or below the Bitterfield rate, lining up service guarantees, and — critically — understanding why the purchasing officer called Nathan by name before we bid. Without that answer, we are guessing what the real objection was. You could reach back to Nathan for anything more he has learned, or contact the district directly to open a conversation about the spring renewal. The work you do this quarter becomes the bid you submit in January.

*Tradeoff*: This is the only path that wins back the main contract, but the revenue does not hit Glenmont's books until spring. The December review would show process progress — a prepared bid, a relationship re-established — not a dollar figure.

**Option C — Both (satellites now + spring bid prep)**

Pursue the satellite sites immediately for this quarter's revenue, while simultaneously investigating the real reason for the switch and preparing the spring bid. The satellite work builds a re-entry point with the district's purchasing officer — you have a reason to call them that is not "why did you leave us" but "we can serve your satellite locations." That conversation may also surface what drove the main contract to Bitterfield, which feeds directly into the January bid.

*Tradeoff*: More work in parallel, but the two tracks reinforce each other. The December review would show both a revenue recovery line (satellites) and a documented bid preparation track (main contract).

---

My recommendation would be Option C — take the satellite ground now while using that contact to investigate and prepare for the spring bid. That gives you something concrete to show in December and a path to full recovery by spring. But it is your call on how you want to approach the district.
